gen-jetbrains-mono-fs-karma: Karma reads classic and trustworthy, with terminals finishing well clear of the stem. JetBrains Mono suits big, brief headings, where its fixed-width, code-style letters and open scissor-blade terminals can stand apart.
gen-jetbrains-mono-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and generous, with big-looking words and an e that opens clearly to the right. Yet JetBrains Mono's loosely strung, rounded-wire letters are the standout, a fixed-width edge against that sturdy body.
gen-jetbrains-mono-switzer: Tubular and Swiss-minded, with c tips that stay apart. Switzer's wire-like letterforms and JetBrains Mono's loosely strung, fixed-width characters share a wiry, stripped-back streak, and that kinship is the strongest thing here.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-hoover: Hoover is refined but robust, with a generous entry into the e's eye. Hoover's compressed ascenders keep company with Luckiest Guy, a cheerful, loud display face with poured-looking ink and a high mean line.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-karma: Luckiest Guy is all cheer and volume, with ink that looks poured and a mean line set high. Karma does the opposite job, trustworthy and classic, with terminals finishing well clear of the stem.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-ranade: Luckiest Guy shouts cheerfully in single-weight outline-like strokes, with its e opening clearly to the right. Ranade's slightly shifting, widely spaced lines then stretch out beneath it, so loud and organic share the page.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans is contemporary and approachable, with wide gaps at its curve ends. Luckiest Guy shouts with a high lowercase, and the step down to moderate lowercase height is where the whole thing comes alive.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-aclonica: Cheerful, blunt and loud: Luckiest Guy has glyphs that look cut from equal-width strips. And in Aclonica a line runs long and stretched-out, its deep midsection and widely spaced letters giving the reading a slow pull.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-cossette-titre: Cossette Titre is contemporary, with open bowls that welcome the eye. Cossette Titre's close-nestled letters and low capitals make a quiet counterweight to Luckiest Guy, whose strokes have no contrast to slow the eye.
gen-luckiest-guy-outfit: Cheerful from the first letter, Luckiest Guy shouts. Outfit's cable-bent curves, never swelling or thinning, feel clean and approachable beside it, a shout settling into conversation as lowercase height drops.
